title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Relevant Person
tiers.description: Any director or company secretary of any Group member; any person with authority and responsibility for planning, direction and control of the Company's activities (KMP); any employee or personnel of, or service provider to, the Investment Manager (including employees and personnel of Regal Partners Limited and its subsidiaries, and contractors/consultants whose engagement incorporates this policy); and any other person the Board determines to be a Relevant Person.

tiers.name: Company Secretary or director of the Company (excluding the Chair)
tiers.description: Distinguished only for Clearance routing: the Chair of the Board is the Clearance Officer, and directors have an additional Appendix 3Y notification duty to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of dealing.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for Clearance routing: the Chair of the Board's Audit and Risk Committee is the Clearance Officer.

tiers.name: Associate
tiers.description: A person over whom a Relevant Person has investment control or influence: a family member (including a child), a nominee (including an investment manager managing funds on the Principal's behalf), a trust of which the Principal, family member or family-controlled company is trustee or beneficiary, a partner, or a company the Principal controls.

definitions.hedging_definition: Derivatives has the meaning given in the Corporations Act and includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities; put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days prior to the scheduled release of half year or full year results, or the announcement of a dividend or other material capital management initiative
windows.end_anchor: commencement of trading on the first trading day after such release or announcement

windows.start_anchor: commencement of on-market share purchases under the performance fee reinvestment mechanism
commencement of on-market share purchases under the Company's dividend reinvestment plan

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine any other period during which Relevant Persons and Associates are not permitted to Deal in Company Securities. Confidentiality of such a Board-determined period is not addressed.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on using any Derivative (which by definition includes put/call options, forward contracts, swaps, CFDs and caps and collars) in relation to unvested Company Securities, to preserve the link between performance hurdles and value realisation.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company Securities.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested Company Securities (whether or not still subject to a holding lock, which the policy does not separately distinguish) are expressly permitted provided the Dealing complies with the balance of the policy, i.e. Clearance, the front page test, and no Inside Information or blackout period.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Same rule as for vested-locked holdings; the policy does not distinguish further once shares have vested.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: 'Hedging' is not a separately defined term but is swept in because 'Derivatives' is defined to include 'any other hedging or investment arrangement', and Derivatives over unvested securities are banned outright.
rules.evidence: Derivatives ... includes ... any other hedging or investment arrangement. [16.2] Relevant Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company Securities.

rules.detail: A hedging arrangement over vested Company Securities is a Derivative and is expressly permitted subject to ordinary clearance and policy compliance.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: A prepaid forward or similar monetisation is a 'forward contract', expressly named within the Derivatives definition, so it is caught by the outright ban on Derivatives over unvested Company Securities.
rules.evidence: Derivatives ... includes ... put or call options, forward contracts, futures ... and any other hedging or investment arrangement. Relevant Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company Securities.

rules.detail: A forward-contract-based monetisation over vested Company Securities is a Derivative and is expressly permitted subject to ordinary Dealing compliance.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Short selling of Company Securities by Relevant Persons is not named anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
Contracts for difference are expressly named within the Derivatives definition, so a CFD over unvested Company Securities is banned outright.
rules.evidence: Derivatives ... includes ... swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.

rules.detail: A CFD over vested Company Securities is a Derivative and is expressly permitted subject to ordinary clearance and policy compliance.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Prohibited by default regardless of vesting status; the Board (not the ordinary Clearance Officer) may expressly permit a margin loan arrangement as an exception.
rules.evidence: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.

rules.detail: Using Company Securities as security against loan repayments is prohibited by default; the same Board-permission carve-out applies as for margin loans.
rules.evidence: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.

rules.detail: The prohibition extends beyond formal margin loans to 'other types of margin lending arrangements' generally; entering any such secured financing is banned by default, subject only to express Board permission.
rules.evidence: Margin loans to support an investment in Company Securities (and other types of margin lending arrangements) can compromise compliance with this policy, as the loan's terms may compel the sale of Company Securities during a blackout period or when the Relevant Person has relevant Inside Information.

rules.detail: Round-trip dealing within 3 months, or other frequent/regular trading, is banned outright as speculative dealing; no waiver mechanism is stated.
rules.evidence: A Relevant Person or Associate must not engage in short term Dealing in Company Securities. Short-term trading includes Dealing in securities within a 3 month period and entering into other short-term dealings in a manner which involves frequent and regular trading activity.

clearance.evidence: A Clearance ... will remain in force for the date of approval only, unless otherwise notified by the Clearance Officer (if the Dealing is not placed within this time, the Clearance will no longer have effect and a new Clearance must be requested and obtained). ... If Clearance is refused by the Clearance Officer, the person who sought the Clearance must keep that information confidential.

clearance.evidence: for the Company Secretary or a director of the Company (excluding the Chair of the Board), the Chair of the Board. ... he or she must ensure that an Appendix 3Y Change of Directors' Interest Notice is completed ... and provided to the Company Secretary within two business days after any Dealing in Company Securities.

clearance.approver: the Chair of the Board's Audit and Risk Committee (as Clearance Officer)
clearance.evidence: for the Chair of the Board, the Chair of the Board's Audit and Risk Committee.

clearance.evidence: for an Associate, the Clearance Officer of his or her Principal.

short_term.basis: round-trip dealing within 3 months (buy then sell, or vice versa); also catches frequent and regular trading activity generally
short_term.evidence: A Relevant Person or Associate must not engage in short term Dealing in Company Securities. Short-term trading includes Dealing in securities within a 3 month period and entering into other short-term dealings in a manner which involves frequent and regular trading activity.

exceptions.evidence: if a person has a pressing financial commitment that cannot otherwise be satisfied and all reasonable alternatives have been investigated.

if a person is required by court order, or enforceable undertaking (eg in a bona fide family settlement) to transfer or sell Company Securities or there is another overriding legal requirement to do so.
undertake a Dealing which is conducted for the purpose of, and in accordance with, the Management Agreement or the performance fee reinvestment mechanism in connection with the Management Agreement.

Deal in Company Securities under an offer or invitation made by the Company to all or most of its ordinary shareholders – such as an offer or invitation under a rights issue, bonus issue, equal access buy-back or in lieu of a cash dividend ... or under an equal reduction of capital undertaken by the Company.

undertake a Dealing which involves or results from an acquisition of Company Securities under a security purchase plan or a dividend reinvestment plan where the Relevant Person or his or her Associate: (i) did not commence or amend their participation in the plan during a blackout period; and (ii) did not withdraw from the plan during a blackout period.

undertake to accept, or accept, an offer for Company Securities made under a takeover bid or dispose of Company Securities under a court-approved compromise or arrangement under Part 5.1 of the Corporations Act.

undertake a Dealing in units of or interests in, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme investing primarily in Company Securities) whereby the assets of that fund or scheme are invested at a third party's sole discretion.
undertake a Dealing of Company Securities as a result of a change in the trustee of a trust.
accept an offer to acquire Company Securities, or acquire Company Securities, under any equity incentive plan that the Board from time to time determines is a plan to which this clause 10.1 applies.

exercise (but not sell Company Securities following exercise) an option or right under an equity incentive plan, or convert a convertible security, where the final date for exercise or conversion falls during a blackout period ... provided that the Clearance Officer has confirmed that the exercise is permitted.
undertake a Dealing which involves or results in the forfeiture, lapse, cancellation or surrender of Company Securities under an equity incentive plan.

undertake a Dealing which involves or results in an off-market transaction involving the transfer or other disposal of Company Securities between a Relevant Person or Associate and any of the following: an Associate of the Relevant Person ... a company, trust or other entity over which the Relevant Person or Associate has control or significant influence ... or a superannuation fund or other pension or saving scheme in which the Relevant Person or an Associate is a beneficiary.
undertake a Dealing in Company Securities or communicate information pursuant to a requirement imposed by law.

exemption_authority: The Clearance Officer (Company Secretary, Chair of the Board, or Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, depending on tier) may grant Clearance to Deal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances: a court order or enforceable undertaking, or a pressing financial commitment that cannot otherwise be satisfied after investigating all reasonable alternatives (a tax liability alone will not generally qualify). Clearance may be refused without reasons, is final and binding, must be kept confidential by the applicant if refused, lapses immediately if Inside Information is acquired, and is valid only for the date of approval. Separately, the Board (not the Clearance Officer) may expressly permit a margin loan or security arrangement that would otherwise be prohibited under clause 17.2.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in the Corporations Act and includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities; put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly names 'caps and collars' as a covered Derivative, confirming a bank-written equity collar over the shares is squarely regulated as a Dealing, and is expressly permitted over vested shares subject to ordinary Clearance rather than left to interpretation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is prohibited by default; the bank should seek specific Board approval (a higher bar than the ordinary Clearance Officer sign-off used for the derivative legs) before the secured loan can proceed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Clearance ... will remain in force for the date of approval only, unless otherwise notified by the Clearance Officer (if the Dealing is not placed within this time, the Clearance will no longer have effect and a new Clearance must be requested and obtained).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Absent a specific extension, a cleared OTC collar trade must be executed the same day it is approved, creating tight execution timing that the bank must plan around.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Dealing in Company Securities or Securities of another entity under this policy must not be made if that Dealing would fail the 'front page' test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a cleared and otherwise permitted collar could still be refused or later criticised on a subjective public-perception basis distinct from the strict legal and policy tests.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin loans to support an investment in Company Securities (and other types of margin lending arrangements) can compromise compliance with this policy, as the loan's terms may compel the sale of Company Securities during a blackout period or when the Relevant Person has relevant Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike some peer policies, there is no exclusion for a lender's forced sale; if the bank enforces the collar's security during a blackout period, that sale would likely be a breach of this policy rather than excluded trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Relevant Person must: inform any Associate of the periods during which the Relevant Person must not Deal in Company Securities; inform any Associate that he or she must not Deal in Company Securities on a speculative basis; and request any Associate to inform the Relevant Person immediately after Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its financing through a family member, trust or controlled entity does not avoid the restrictions; the Relevant Person remains responsible for the Associate's compliance.

summary: The derivative legs of a funded collar are achievable under this policy: 'Derivatives' is expressly defined to include 'caps and collars', and section 16.3 permits Relevant Persons to use Derivatives over vested Company Securities provided the Dealing otherwise complies with the policy — prior written Clearance from the applicable Clearance Officer (Company Secretary, or the Chair of the Board or Audit and Risk Committee Chair for more senior tiers), passing the 'front page' test, made outside blackout periods and while not in possession of Inside Information; Clearance is valid only for the day it is granted, so execution timing is tight. The loan leg is the key obstacle: margin loans and any arrangement using Company Securities as security for loan repayments are prohibited by default under section 17.2, and can only proceed if the Board (not the ordinary Clearance Officer) expressly permits the arrangement; if the bank were to enforce that security and force a sale during a blackout period, that sale is not carved out as excluded trading and would likely breach the policy. Unvested Company Securities cannot be used for either the derivative or the collateral leg at all. Subject to specific Board approval for the secured loan, standard Clearance Officer approval for the collar itself, avoidance of the 3-month short-term dealing rule and blackout windows, and appropriate handling of any Associate involvement, a funded collar over vested shares is workable.
